chunks: My father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and others, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, who said:

I saw Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrive at the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he placed his hand on it and said: I ask Allah, who selected you and chose you and guided you and guided (creation) through you, to send His blessings upon you.
Then he said: Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet.
O you who believe! Send your blessings on him and salute him with all respect.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq do when visiting the grave of the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the theological basis for visiting the Prophet's grave by demonstrating Imam al-Sadiq’s (a.s.) direct practice of touching the grave while supplicating, thereby validating the physical aspect of Ziyarah. It connects the believer's invocation to the Quranic command of Salawat, illustrating how the Ahl al-Bayt embody the verse 'Indeed, Allah confers blessing upon the Prophet, and His angels [as well]' (33:56) by serving as the means through which divine blessings flow to the community.
